issue_context.title: Debug Info: ptype showing wrong modifiers?
comments: Update: It looks like we are picking up the modifiers from [the substitute method](https://github.com/oracle/graal/blob/d465c5885127caef6d551d417e6caef937fe225a/substratevm/src/com.oracle.svm.core/src/com/oracle/svm/core/jdk/JavaLangSubstitutions.java#L92-L96) instead of the original. I've got a fix and working on extending the `debuginfotest` to catch such issues both for methods and fields.

Hmm, that's an interesting issue.

When we present the source code in the debugger we will actually be displaying the substituted method code. So, from the point of view of someone stepping through the implementation marking it as private matches the displayed view.

However, from the point of view of someone stepping into a call to the original method from a caller in some other class than the original (or, indeed, substituted) owner it really ought to look like a public method.

I think you are right that it would be clearest if the permissions displayed in the ptype listing reflected the original. A disparity when looking at a subsituted implementation is going to be understandable by virtue of the fact that the displayed method is clearly a replacement. A disparity at the point of call has no accompanying info in the source to explain the disparity.

review_comments: I was not able to test this path with my tests. Recommendations are welcome!

Me neither.

Looking at how AnnotationSubstituionProcessor is implemented it looks like you need both a target class and target field labelled with a Substitute annotation (also, probably a TargetElement annotation on the field). If you try using a Substitute annotation on the field when the class just has a TargetClass annotation then you get an error saying you need to use Inject, Delete or Alias on the field. However, I am not 100% clear what the difference is supposed to be between labelling a class with TargetClass vs labelling it with Substitute. I think it is something to do with whether fields that are not explicitly targeted get copied across.

> However, I am not 100% clear what the difference is supposed to be between labelling a class with TargetClass vs labelling it with Substitute. I think it is something to do with whether fields that are not explicitly targeted get copied across.

This seems to be covered in https://github.com/oracle/graal/blob/6a8914b68f1709e90c98f9dbd2134d854b2efbf5/substratevm/src/com.oracle.svm.core/src/com/oracle/svm/core/annotate/TargetClass.java#L64-L69

The difference is essentially that in a Class annotated with `TargetClass` you may only `Substitute` the methods you want and the rest of the original methods will be available, on the other hand in a Class annotated with `Substitute` as well all the original methods are deleted and only methods annotated with `Substitute` or `KeepOriginal` are now available.
Yeah, that's the comment I was vaguely remembering having read. When I said fields above I really meant to say members.
I was not able to test this path with my tests. Recommendations are welcome!

@zakkak, as @peter-hofer reminded me, a more elegant way to get the original modifiers would be to use `hostedMethod.getJavaMethod()` which uses the `OriginalMethodProvider` interface to accomplish the same thing. 

Please give that a try.
